subject: physics
question_text: Define unit vector, null vector and position vector.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), SHORT ANSWER ***3 of Unit 4, three-star. SHIPS WITH ONE CUT ON PURPOSE: three definitions are a 4-mark answer and nothing else. Padding them to an 8-mark LAQ would teach a student to write twice what the question pays for, which is the opposite of what this book is for — and TS IPE Section C is drawn from the long derivations, not from definitions. The engine hides the length switch by itself when a question declares a single cut. The 1/1/2 split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Unit vector
lines: A vector whose magnitude is one unit
The unit vectors along the x, y and z
axes are written i, j and k.
steps.margin_note: Write the formula, not only the sentence. "Magnitude one" and Â = A/|A| are what the examiner ticks.
steps.why: A vector carries a size and a direction together. Dividing by its own magnitude strips the size away and leaves the direction alone, which is the only thing a unit vector is for.
common_mistakes: Saying a unit vector has magnitude one unit of the same quantity — it has no unit at all.
Writing Â = A without the magnitude in the denominator.

recall.must_convey: That a unit vector has magnitude one and is A divided by the magnitude of A.
accept: a vector of magnitude one is a unit vector
unit vector is A by mod A
it gives only the direction
magnitude one unnadi, direction matrame cheptundi
A cap equals A by magnitude of A
reject: drawn from the origin to the point
heard_as: i cap j cap k cap

steps.memory_tip: The definition is a division: the vector over its own magnitude. Size 1, direction kept.

steps.label: Null vector
lines: A vector whose magnitude is zero is
called a null vector or zero vector.
steps.margin_note: Say that the direction is not defined. That sentence is what separates a null vector from an ordinary one.
steps.why: Adding a vector to its own negative has to give something, and that something cannot point anywhere. The null vector is what keeps vector addition closed.
common_mistakes: Saying the direction is zero — a direction cannot be zero, it is undefined.
Writing the answer as the number 0 instead of the zero vector.

recall.must_convey: That a null vector has zero magnitude and an undefined direction.
accept: a vector whose magnitude is zero
null vector, zero magnitude, direction not defined
A plus minus A gives the null vector
zero vector ani kuda antaru
its direction is arbitrary or undefined
reject: from the origin to the point P

steps.memory_tip: Think A + (−A): the size is zero and no direction is left. That is the null vector.

steps.label: Position vector
lines: The vector drawn from the origin O to
a point P gives the position of P.
It is called the position vector of P.
steps.margin_note: Name the origin. A position vector means nothing until you say what it is measured from.
steps.why: A point on its own has no direction or distance attached to it. Joining it to a chosen origin turns a location into a vector you can add and resolve.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the origin, which makes the vector meaningless.
Confusing it with displacement, which joins two points, not the origin and a point.

recall.must_convey: That the position vector is drawn from the origin to the point.
accept: drawn from the origin to the point
position vector of P is O P
it gives the position of the particle from the origin
origin nunchi point varaku
the vector joining the origin and the point

steps.memory_tip: Always drawn FROM the origin TO the point. The origin end never moves.

steps.label: Sketch (extra)
steps.margin_note: Not marked on a definitions question. A twenty-second sketch — draw it only if the words are already down.
steps.why: The three coordinates are hard to picture from the formula alone. Dropping P to the plane at F and then to the axes is what shows where x, y and z each come from.
common_mistakes: Spending exam time on a careful 3-D box for a question that marks the words, not the picture.

recall.must_convey: That a sketch is drawn. Naming it is full credit.

steps.memory_tip: Draw the box: drop P to the xy-plane, then to the x-axis. The three coordinates appear as three edges.

steps.label: In component form
lines: If P has coordinates (x, y, z), then

lines.text: OP = r = x i + y j + z k

steps.margin_note: Box the magnitude. Put the caps on i, j and k by hand — they are unit vectors, not numbers.
steps.why: Writing the position vector in components is what lets you actually compute with it — the magnitude then follows straight from Pythagoras in three dimensions.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the unit vectors and writing r = x + y + z.
Forgetting the square root in the magnitude.

recall.must_convey: That r = x i + y j + z k and |r| = root of (x² + y² + z²).
accept: r equals x i cap plus y j cap plus z k cap

the magnitude comes from Pythagoras
heard_as: i cap j cap k cap

steps.memory_tip: r = xi + yj + zk, and the magnitude is the square root of the three squares.
